policy: New history is authorized. The chosen serial order is canonical at every speed. Calendar obligations keep their due dates; ordinary decisions should become daily as mixed quantities/durations are separated and input-revision paths made cheap.
limitations: Human boundary/helper/alias survey plus source-call inventory, not a formal complete interprocedural proof. Dynamic callbacks, property accessors, class methods and conditional effects require review. Observed old-order edges below are evidence, not constraints on the redesigned simulation.

survey.name: ownershipTick
survey.cadence_at_survey: Every day. Builds W._pm with folkIndex; for every settlement refreshes householdsOf, initializes ownership/legacy larder, and binds field/building title accessors. ownersRetire runs only when day()%30===0. No settlement dueOn staggering.
reads: W.settlements order and s.folk; W.households and membership; s._owners / legacy s._lard; W.caravans for owner-retirement exclusions; W.clock.day.
writes: W._pm (derived whole-realm person index); s.households/_householdsD/_householdsN and household membership caches; s._owners, household account / population maps, and possible initial held-food migration; accessor bindings on s.furl and s.buildings; monthly owner-record deletion/retirement.
survey.aliases: Household balances are authoritative household assets with person-facing purse proxies; ownership inventories may be exposed through commodity account proxies. Binding f.own/f.wk and b.ownerId redirects to f.title / b.title. Initialization can move old unowned/larder stores into household and lord claims, so alias setup is not read-only. Retiring an empty extinct household removes its owner record across settlements but leaves W.households and its successor chain.
survey.rng: None directly. This phase is before all RNG-consuming phases and establishes the baseline call order.
survey.ordered_records: No direct jot/annal or ID allocation found. Ownership init can set up storage/account state; it preserves source household order.
survey.transitive_helpers: folkIndex scans settlements and nonempty households; householdsOf may reuse same-day membership cache; initOwnership migrates old larder stock and initializes each owner; bindPropertyRights installs live getters/setters; ownersRetire checks caravan loads, all settlements and storage holds before dropping empty records.
observed_order_at_survey: Must precede every listed economy/population/market/tenure/household consumer: they rely on W._pm, household membership, initialized owner claims and title aliases.
Must precede storage/account operations that can encounter household owner aliases; moving it later changes legacy larder conversion and what owner records exist.
survey.cache_or_preparation: W._pm is deliberately reused in tickPopulation; tickTenure currently makes its own folkIndex and kin indexes. A shared view could be built once only if later phases preserve membership invalidation and cannot observe a different point-in-day population.

survey.name: tickWeather
survey.cadence_at_survey: Every day, no due guard. Decrements W.weather.t; on expiry (t<=0) changes weather and resets duration. Snowpack is season/state dependent; flooding/eclipses decay when positive.
reads: W.weather.t/state/wind; seasonIdx(); W.drought; W.snowpack, W.flooding, W.eclipse.
writes: W.weather state/t/wind; W.snowpack; W.flooding; W.eclipse.
survey.aliases: World-global weather and environment, not a settlement record. Other systems read W.drought and weather; this function itself changes snowpack/flooding/eclipses.
survey.rng: On expiration only: rand(sim) at line 11882, chance(sim, .25) conditionally at 11884, randi(sim,5) and rand(sim) at 11887-88. Chance draw is conditional on the rainy branch.
survey.ordered_records: No direct journal/annal/ID effects. Its conditional sim-stream draw count affects later sim consumers.
survey.transitive_helpers: seasonIdx, rand/randi/chance; chance uses RS[st]() and frand uses rand(folk) (index.html:830-833,3431).
observed_order_at_survey: Keep before later same-day shared `sim` stream consumers: weather transition draws are conditional, so relocating them can shift any later consumer reached that day. tickWeather’s mutated state (weather, snowpack, flooding, eclipse) is read by intervening phases (e.g. military/land); tickEconomy directly reads season and W.drought, not tickWeather’s state.
survey.cache_or_preparation: Season index is pure for a fixed day/calendar and is recomputed by other phases; sharing the value is safe only as a read-only same-day scalar. Do not hoist random weather transition decisions.

survey.name: tickEconomy
survey.cadence_at_survey: Every day for every settlement; the seasonal yield multiplier is selected daily. Once per calendar year (first visit where _shopY!==year) recounts smithies/dyers/vine plots; once per autumn seasonIdx()==2 vintages are added. Monthly army/watch payments and crown transfer run on day()%30===0. Trade only runs on even days and internally visits half the settlement indexes per even day. Arrivals and road volume/upkeep accrual are checked daily.
reads: World drought/land/season/modifiers; settlement resources, population/plague/siege, fields, buildings, owners, household ledger, stores and prices; current caravans/routes, armies, roads; purse means and global tax/crown ledger.
writes: Settlement stocks and _made output; storage facility/carriage state/report; owner-held inventory, offers and spoilage; workshop counts and outputs; caravan list/arrival days/tradeV; roads vol/_wv; army and watch arrears; monthly soldier/watch pay, treasury/book/cash records, capital _poolCash.
survey.aliases: With commodity balances active, s.stores and per-owner held/sale views resolve through the StorageLedger, and s._owners claims track the same physical stock. `consumeOwned`, `offer`, `spoilOwned`, purchase and arrival helpers update stock, reserve, market indexes, and canonical storage outcomes together. Household fuel/tools/cloth/wine use is debited from household-held inventory here; food is left to tickPopulation. Money uses household assets/proxies, houses, Crown treasury, and account ledgers.
survey.rng: Conditional `chance(sim,...)` for plague transmission on caravan arrival (12421). tickTrade itself can trigger helper randomness through merchant/driver selection and other transitive routines; route/trade order and simTick position must be retained. No frand direct in tickEconomy body.
survey.ordered_records: Storage mutations append canonical storage outcomes; transfers/books/cash records for trades and monthly payroll; annals on plague arrival; storage investment can allocate facility IDs. Caravans receive cargo IDs through storageCargo paths. Results depend on current call/iteration order.
survey.transitive_helpers: storageInit, storageTick (routes exposed goods and charges handling), storageInvestment, landYield, made; initOwnership; consumeOwned; spoilOwned; tickTrade -> tradeOnTheWay/route/freight/wayToll/ladeOut/purchase/driverFor and caravan creation; arrival -> storageCargoArrive/ladeIn/tolls/taxes/offers; monthly soldiersPay/payWatch/cashRecord.
observed_order_at_survey: tickWeather must remain before any later shared `sim` RNG consumer: weather makes conditional sim-stream draws, while economy can conditionally consume `sim` on caravan plague arrival (12421). No direct tickWeather-state → tickEconomy data edge was established; economy reads season and W.drought (12374–12382).
tickEconomy -> tickPopulation: daily production, spoilage, trade arrivals and owner food stock precede household consumption; population stores hunger/fill/wealth from resulting stock.
tickEconomy -> tickMarket: market reconciles output and owner stock after daily production/trade/consumption.
tickEconomy -> commoditySettleAll: all changes must enter daily storage journal after day mutators.
survey.cache_or_preparation: Potential bounded read prep: a same-day settlement-index schedule mask and simple environmental scalars. Storage route/facility helpers already maintain private reusable route/index caches; a day-start inventory snapshot is unsafe because purchases, consumption and arrivals alter live availability in canonical order.

survey.name: tickPopulation
survey.cadence_at_survey: Every day, every settlement, in array order. No due guard. Housing capacity is recomputed if unset or day()%10===0; otherwise cached _room is used. Per-settlement plague progression runs when infected>0.3; famine event only on hunger>0.4 and !famineFlag and pop>100.
reads: Settlement food stocks and owner/household population ledger; fields/land/market neighbors/buildings for carrying capacity; current prosperity, pop, tradeV, siege/quarantine/festival, infection/recovery; W._pm when initialized by ownershipTick.
writes: Household population Map entries and hunger; s.hunger, _room, cap/K, pop repair floor, recovered, unrest, prosperity/prosT, tradeV decay, famineFlag, infection/recovery/plagueDead/pyres; W.legitimacy and W.plagueActive.
Famine helper may kill people, alter ownership/claims, population membership, stock and annals.
survey.aliases: Household population is a settlement-keyed ledger on household accounts, not a copy of person count; s.pop is a separate aggregate. eatHouseholds initializes ownership if needed, credits the food output, reconciles owner stock, tops up relief, consumes stock, and writes household hunger/fill/wealth summaries. `householdsOf` supplies the settlement list; household membership changes invalidate cached population totals.
survey.rng: Conditional randi(sim,3) only when famine transition occurs; famineStrikes is transitive and can consume further randomness/change households. No everyday random demographic sample: births/deaths are deterministic arithmetic.
survey.ordered_records: emit adds annal history and W.house news when famine/burnout events occur. Famine strike helper may allocate/retire people and update person/index/IDs.
survey.transitive_helpers: eatHouseholds -> initOwnership/shareOutput/reconcile/topUpFood/eatFood; housing; carryingCap -> marketHeads and settlementDistanceWeights; publicOrderSuppression; famineStrikes; emit/vary on famine text.
observed_order_at_survey: tickEconomy -> tickPopulation, because it produces/spoils/transports food before eatHouseholds.

tickPopulation -> tickMarket in simTick order: market computes `_pl` from current s.pop/price and its due-settlement transaction reads current household/account state after this day’s population and intervening phases; tickMarket is invoked after population, although it returns early if no monthly settlement is due.

tickPopulation -> tickTenure in the current order: annual tenure reads current prosperity/household and world state after population and intervening phases; population’s conditional famine `sim` draws also precede later RNG consumers.
ownershipTick -> tickPopulation for W._pm and claims.
survey.cache_or_preparation: A read-only settlement distance-weight cache is already used by carryingCap. Could share per-day `folkIndex` and due-independent household enumeration only while honoring invalidations from famine/migration and avoiding whole-day population snapshots.

survey.name: tickMarket
survey.cadence_at_survey: Builds due mask by dueOn(si,30,11); each settlement is due exactly when (day()+si*11)%30===0, then returns before work if none. For each due settlement, order is shareOutput, reconcile, homeward, provision, waifs, payCrafts, storage settleStores, reprice, local freight-rate adjustment. After those due settlements, recomputes realm `_pl` from all positive-pop settlements every invocation (even no due settlement returns early before this calculation).
reads: Per settlement stores/owners/output and current monthly prices/worth; household heads/membership/wealth/population/roles; market offers/reserves and routes, nearby trade counts/markets; current _pl and prices; all positive-pop settlement prices/pop for realm level.
writes: Owner and household stock via offers/purchases/consumption; sale/reserve/market maps; household wealth and credit; craft pools and unmet wants; monthly prices `_pxY`/`px`; `_wait`, freight rates; storage settlements; realm wage/price level `_pl`; possibly market trade/household cached data.
survey.aliases: `shareOutput` transfers unassigned yield into named owner claims and offers. `reconcile` synchronizes ownership ledger with physical settlement stock. `provision` draws household purse/credit and consumes/creates market stock. `waifs` transfers departed/dead seller stock to lord. Household `w`/`assets.w` is shared with yearly household decisions and account totals; stock views proxy the common StorageLedger; mkt/rsv maps refer to same balances.
survey.rng: No obvious direct RNG in tickMarket, but transitive storage/market/reprice helpers should be checked if candidate extraction changes calls; current body’s order is canonical.
survey.ordered_records: Purchases/flows/book transfers and storage journal outcomes; reprice updates price history; storage settleStores may generate spoilage events; no direct emit/ID in body.
survey.transitive_helpers: shareOutput, reconcile, homeward, provision (goodWorth/foodDays/purchase/credit/pay/work), waifs, payCrafts, storage.settleStores, reprice, price; dueOn. `dueOn` is `(day()+si*salt)%period===0` (14309).
observed_order_at_survey: tickTenure -> tickMarket in simTick order: if a settlement is due in both routines that day, market provisions read after tenure’s same-day rent/tax/land/purse writes. Other due dates read the latest earlier tenure result.

tickPopulation -> tickMarket in simTick order: when market runs, its realm `_pl` recomputation uses current s.pop and due transactions see the current post-population and intervening-phase household/account state. If no market settlement is due anywhere, tickMarket returns before recomputing `_pl`.
tickEconomy -> tickMarket: current daily production, offers, spoilage, non-food use and arrivals are inputs.
tickMarket -> tickHouseholds over the chronology: household annual choices read the latest market prices/stock/wealth/freight; on a coincident due day the market runs first.
tickMarket -> commoditySettleAll: daily market storage changes must be settled after them.
survey.cache_or_preparation: The due mask is pure and could be shared with any exact same `(day, settlement order, 30, 11)` consumer. Reuse existing `folkIndex`, trade-count and route caches, but no capture of offer quantities across settlement visits: earlier settlements or purchases mutate availability.

survey.name: tickTenure
survey.cadence_at_survey: No-op if !W.land. Per-settlement annual mask: dueOn(si,360,37). Before return, each nonannual settlement due on dueOn(si,90,37) runs farmQuarters. Annual due settlements then execute full tenure pass. Final realm-level yeoman annal decision is conditional on a large buyer and frand()<.3.
reads: W.land, settlement order, land field tenure/owner/work state, person index and parent/spouse genealogy; households/heads/pop sizes, purse/debt/assets, `_pl`, current/year grain prices, customs/taxes, current prices, buildings and parish/mill.
writes: Quarterly farm state; field owner/work/tenure, admission/sale/letting journal and drawing dirty calls; household debt/purse and landlord transfers; rent/tax and house/Crown ledgers; household strip/crop/ha counts; _ltY/_lt; annual grain output assumptions; may write annal.
survey.aliases: Furlong `own` / `wk` are accessors bound by ownershipTick to title owner/work references; direct writes change `f.title`. Household head purse resolves to household-account assets, so rent/tax/sale/debt operations change wealth seen in every other phase. `lordAcct`/transfer/book/cashRecord update shared house/crown ledgers.
survey.rng: `frand()` uses folk stream (3431): per vacant-strip bidder choice, debtor strip selection, and final yeoman annal. Iteration/order affects draw assignment.
survey.ordered_records: `courtLand`/writeFurlong can append land/admission outcomes; transfers/entry fines/hearth tax/book/cash changes are canonical; final emit is annal when threshold passes. No object-ID allocation evident in main loop.
survey.transitive_helpers: farmQuarters, folkIndex, parent/spouse indexing, chooseLandUse, headsOf/householdHead, manorYear, courtHolding, heirOf, entryFine, stripBidder, courtLand, settleTenure, manorRents, farmMills, rent/price transfer, repay, landValue, writeFurlong, life/emit/vary.
observed_order_at_survey: ownershipTick -> tickTenure: title accessors, owner claims, household identities and W._pm inputs.
tickPopulation -> tickTenure in simTick order: tenure reads current prosperity/household state after population and intervening phases.
tickTenure -> tickMarket in simTick order: when market and annual tenure are due on the same day, market reads tenure’s same-day writes.
tickTenure reads current `_pl` and `yearPrice(s,"grain")`; because tenure precedes market, these values come from the latest prior market update, not the market pass later in that same simTick.
survey.cache_or_preparation: Can precompute the exact 360-day and 90-day due masks from one day/order/salt without modifying behavior. The function already builds a single PM plus parent→children and spouse maps; their order matters and could be shared only if invalidation/first-seen ordering remains identical.

survey.name: tickHouseholds
survey.cadence_at_survey: No-op if !W.fams. Due mask dueOn(si,360,29); returns if none. Rebuilds W._pm and child index once per call, then annual household work for each due settlement with nonempty folk.
reads: All settlement people and households, parent/child/kin graphs, current market prices and stocks, price level, trade income/jobs, household purse/debt/needs/herds/home/land/ownership, lord purse/stock, roads/settlements/quarantine/siege, farm/wood/water sites.
writes: Household/person membership, household assets and person-facing wealth; marriage/house formation and migration; s.pop/mig counters; purchases and stock claims, rent and debt repayment; herds/family herd and beast ownership; job/trade choices; land/homes/buildings, work and storage/account transfers; annual lux/pool state.
survey.aliases: `frand` choices are in folk stream; household money and household account wealth alias; `householdAccount`, `pantry`, `herdOf`, `purchase`, `commodityCreditPurchase` update shared balances/claims; person `own`, spouse and child links change census/cache membership. House construction changes building ownership and land-local stock/work.
survey.rng: Many conditional `frand()` draws from folk stream in child house founding, destination choice, annual job values, apprenticeship, family migration, etc. Exact loop/head/trade order is essential. Some text emits add annals.
